people.name: Alcuin of York
people.bio: Northumbrian scholar who ran the York cathedral school, led Charlemagne's palace school and ended his life as abbot of Saint-Martin at Tours.

stops.note: Born in or near York; Britannica gives c. 732.
Pupil at the cathedral school founded by Archbishop Ecgberht, under the master Aelbert.
Directed the school after Aelbert became archbishop in 767 (Britannica dates his headship to 778); built up its library.
Met Charlemagne at Parma and accepted his invitation to the Frankish court.
Master of the palace school, teaching Charlemagne, his family and court; in Aachen 782-790 and 793-796.
Returned to England on church business; again on a mission for Charlemagne in 790.
Abbot of Saint-Martin, where he built up a model monastic school.
Died 19 May 804.

people.name: Aelbert of York
people.bio: Master of the York cathedral school and teacher of Alcuin; became Archbishop of York in 767.

people.name: Peter of Pisa
people.bio: Lombard deacon, grammarian and poet who taught Latin grammar to Charlemagne at the Frankish court.

stops.note: Known in Lombardy for public disputations; Alcuin heard him dispute at Pavia as a young man.

Came to Charlemagne's court after the fall of the Lombard kingdom (773-774) and taught the king grammar for several years; the atlas end date of 799 is uncertain, since he died in Lombardy before 799.

people.name: Charlemagne
people.bio: King of the Franks and emperor, who gathered scholars at his court and studied grammar and the liberal arts with them.

people.name: Paul the Deacon
people.bio: Lombard monk and historian, author of the History of the Lombards, who spent several years at Charlemagne's court before returning to Monte Cassino.

stops.note: Born in Friuli to a noble Lombard family.
Probably educated at the court of King Ratchis in Pavia under the grammarian Flavianus.
At the court of Duke Arichis of Benevento.
Monk at Monte Cassino.
In Charlemagne's retinue from 782.
Wrote the history of the bishops of Metz at the request of Bishop Angilram.
Returned to Monte Cassino after 787 and wrote there.
Most likely died at Monte Cassino on 13 April, probably 799.

people.name: Flavianus
people.bio: Grammarian at the Lombard court of Pavia, named as the teacher of Paul the Deacon.

people.name: Einhard
people.bio: Frankish courtier, builder and biographer of Charlemagne, educated at Fulda and the palace school.

stops.note: Early training at Fulda; Abbot Baugulf sent him to court. Years approximate.
Completed his education at the palace school under Alcuin, then served Charlemagne and Louis the Pious, overseeing buildings at Aachen and Ingelheim.
Sent to Rome to obtain papal approval of Charlemagne's partition of the empire.
Withdrew from court in 830; founded the abbey of Seligenstadt and served as abbot.
Died 14 March 840.

people.name: Theodulf of Orléans
people.bio: Visigothic scholar and poet at Charlemagne's court who became Bishop of Orléans and encouraged schools in his diocese.

stops.note: Joined Charlemagne's court before 794, where he ranked with Alcuin among its most learned members.
Bishop of Orléans from c. 798; encouraged schools in his diocese.
Deposed in 818 on suspicion of joining King Bernard's conspiracy and exiled to Angers.
Died 18 December 821.

people.name: Hrabanus Maurus
people.bio: Benedictine teacher, abbot of Fulda and Archbishop of Mainz, called the 'teacher of Germany'.

stops.note: Born at Mainz c. 776 or 784.
Studied theology and the liberal arts under Alcuin, who named him 'Maurus'; recalled after a year.
Teacher and then head of the monastic school of Fulda.
Abbot of Fulda 822-842.
Retired to the Petersberg after resigning the abbacy.
Archbishop of Mainz from 847; his synod of 848 condemned Gottschalk.
Died at Winkel near Mainz, 4 February 856.

people.name: Gottschalk of Orbais
people.bio: Saxon monk and theologian condemned for his teaching on double predestination.

stops.note: Given as a child oblate to Fulda; made a monk against his will under Abbot Hrabanus.
Released from his vows by the Council of Mainz (June 829), a decision later reversed.
Monk of Orbais (diocese of Soissons), where he studied Augustine on grace and predestination.
Spread his doctrine in Italy, staying with Count Eberhard of Friuli in 846, and returned via Dalmatia, Pannonia and Noricum.
Condemned by the Council of Mainz, 1 October 848.
Imprisoned for life at Hautvillers after the synod of Quierzy (849).
Probably died 30 October 868 or 869.

people.name: Dungal
people.bio: Irish scholar in the Frankish empire, consulted by Charlemagne on astronomy and appointed master of the school of Pavia.

stops.note: Irish scholar at Saint-Denis; wrote to Charlemagne explaining the eclipse of 810.
Appointed master of the school at Pavia by imperial decree in 825.
Probably spent his last years at Bobbio, to which he bequeathed his books.

people.name: Walafrid Strabo
people.bio: Swabian monk and poet, tutor of Charles the Bald and abbot of Reichenau.

stops.note: Educated at Reichenau under Tatto, Erlebald and Wetti.
Studied at Fulda under Hrabanus Maurus.
Tutor to the young Charles the Bald at the court of Louis the Pious.
Abbot of Reichenau from 838.
Driven out for supporting Lothar; fled to Speyer.
Restored as abbot, which he remained until his death (18 August 849).

people.name: Wetti of Reichenau
people.bio: Monk and teacher at Reichenau.

people.name: Erlebald of Reichenau
people.bio: Teacher and abbot of Reichenau, succeeded by Walafrid Strabo in 838.

people.name: Tatto of Reichenau
people.bio: Teacher at Reichenau.

people.name: Lupus of Ferrières
people.bio: Abbot of Ferrières and humanist letter-writer who collected and corrected classical manuscripts.

stops.note: Began his education at Ferrières under Aldric.
Completed his education under Hrabanus Maurus; became a friend and disciple of Einhard.
Nominated abbot of Ferrières on 22 November 840.
Attended the Council of Soissons.

people.name: Aldric of Ferrières
people.bio: Pupil of Alcuin who became abbot of Ferrières and taught Lupus there.

people.name: John Scottus Eriugena
people.bio: Irish philosopher at the court of Charles the Bald, translator of Pseudo-Dionysius and author of the Periphyseon.

stops.note: At the court of Charles the Bald by c. 850/51 (the first certain record, later than the atlas start of 845); wrote on predestination (c. 851), translated Dionysius (c. 860-862) and celebrated Charles's new church at Compiègne in 875.

people.name: Constantine-Cyril the Philosopher
people.bio: Byzantine scholar from Thessalonica who, with his brother Methodius, became the 'Apostle of the Slavs'.

stops.note: Named as a student of Leo the Mathematician; the years and the teaching of philosophy follow the atlas and are not confirmed by the sources used.
Died 14 February 869.

people.name: Photios
people.bio: Byzantine scholar, teacher and twice Patriarch of Constantinople, author of the Bibliotheca.

stops.note: Born c. 815 (other estimates c. 810 to 827).
Embassy 'to the Assyrians', apparently to the caliph.
Taught grammar, philosophy and theology to students; the source describes the teaching as given in his own house.
Patriarch of Constantinople from Christmas 857 until his removal in 867.
Deposed and banished to a monastery at Stenos.
Recalled as tutor to Basil I's son; patriarch again 877-886.

people.name: Notker Balbulus
people.bio: Monk of St Gall, poet of liturgical sequences and teacher in its school.

stops.note: Educated at St Gall under Iso and the Irishman Moengal, with Tuotilo.
Taught at St Gall; librarian in 890 and master of guests 892-894.

people.name: Iso of St Gall
people.bio: Teacher at the monastery school of St Gall.

people.name: Moengal
people.bio: Irish monk and teacher at St Gall.

people.name: Notker Labeo
people.bio: Monk of St Gall who translated and commented on Latin school texts in Old High German.

stops.note: Came to St Gall as a boy.
Devoted himself to teaching.

people.name: Heiric of Auxerre
people.bio: Benedictine monk and teacher who made the school of Saint-Germain at Auxerre famous.

stops.note: Studied at Ferrières under Lupus, after study at Fulda under a pupil of Hrabanus. Years approximate.
Master of the school of his monastery, succeeded by Remigius in 876.

people.name: Remigius of Auxerre
people.bio: Benedictine teacher and commentator who taught at Auxerre, Reims and Paris.

stops.note: Studied under Heiric at Saint-Germain.
Succeeded Heiric as master in 876.
Called to Reims by Archbishop Fulco c. 883 to restore the cathedral school (earlier than the atlas start of 893).
Probably moved to Paris after Fulco's death in 900; his school there is the first recorded in the city.

people.name: Dunchad of Reims
people.bio: Irish teacher named as a master of Remigius of Auxerre.

people.name: Odo of Cluny
people.bio: Abbot of Cluny who studied under Remigius of Auxerre in Paris.

people.name: Asser
people.bio: Welsh monk of St Davids who joined Alfred the Great's court, wrote his Life and became Bishop of Sherborne.

stops.note: Brought up and educated in the clerical community of St Davids; later its bishop.
Entered Alfred's service c. 884, dividing his year between the court and St Davids; given charge of Devon and Cornwall and later made Bishop of Sherborne.

people.name: Bruno of Cologne
people.bio: Brother of Otto I, royal chancellor and Archbishop of Cologne, known as Bruno the Great.

stops.note: Studied at the cathedral school of Utrecht.
Educated at Otto's court school; chancellor from 940.
Accompanied Otto to Italy.
Archbishop of Cologne and Duke of Lorraine.
Died on a mission to France.

people.name: Gerbert of Aurillac
people.bio: Teacher of mathematics and logic at Reims who became Pope Sylvester II.

stops.note: Born at Belliac (now Saint-Simon) near Aurillac.
Monk of Saint-Géraud, studying under Raymond de Lavaur.
Three years at the cathedral school of Vic under Bishop Atto.
Taken to Rome by Count Borrell; met Pope John XIII and became tutor to Otto I's son.
Studied logic with Garamnus, then headed the cathedral school under Archbishop Adalbero.
Won a disputation against Otric of Magdeburg before Otto II.
Abbot of Bobbio.
Returned to Reims; archbishop 991-995.
Archbishop of Ravenna.
Pope Sylvester II from 9 April 999.
Died 12 May 1003.

people.name: Raymond de Lavaur
people.bio: Monk of Saint-Géraud at Aurillac, Gerbert's first teacher.

people.name: Atto of Vic
people.bio: Bishop of Vic under whom Gerbert studied.

people.name: Garamnus
people.bio: Logician with whom Gerbert studied logic at Reims.

people.name: Richer of Saint-Remi
people.bio: Monk of Reims and historian, pupil of Gerbert.

people.name: Abbo of Fleury
people.bio: Monk and abbot of Fleury, scholar of mathematics and astronomy, who also directed the school of Ramsey in England.

stops.note: Born near Orléans.
Called to England to direct the school of the new monastery of Ramsey; the source gives no years.
Abbot of Fleury, his election confirmed with Gerbert's help; the source gives no year.
Killed while trying to restore discipline at La Réole.

people.name: Aimoin of Fleury
people.bio: Monk of Fleury, disciple and biographer of Abbo.

people.name: Fulbert of Chartres
people.bio: Pupil of Gerbert who made the cathedral school of Chartres a leading centre of learning and became its bishop.

stops.note: Studied at Reims under Gerbert.
Opened a school at Chartres in 990; chancellor of the church of Chartres.
Bishop of Chartres from 1007.
Died 10 April 1028 or 1029.

people.name: Berengar of Tours
people.bio: Theologian and pupil of Fulbert at Chartres.

people.name: Lanfranc
people.bio: Lawyer from Pavia who taught at Avranches and Bec and became Archbishop of Canterbury under William the Conqueror.

stops.note: Trained and worked as a lawyer before leaving Italy; years approximate.
Founded a school at Avranches.
Monk of Bec; after three years of seclusion became prior and taught in its school.
First abbot of Saint-Étienne, Caen.
Archbishop of Canterbury; reorganised the English church.

people.name: Anselm of Canterbury
people.bio: Monk, prior and abbot of Bec and later Archbishop of Canterbury, author of the ontological argument.

stops.note: Left home at 23 and travelled through Burgundy and France before reaching Normandy in 1059.
Novice at Bec under Lanfranc, prior and head of its school.
Prior of Bec from 1063, abbot from 1078.
Archbishop of Canterbury; in exile 1097-1100 and 1103-1107.

people.name: Anselm of Laon
people.bio: Theologian whose school at Laon was the most famous in France around 1100; teacher of Abelard.

stops.note: Educated at Bec under Anselm of Canterbury.
Taught in Paris from 1076.
Returned to Laon around the end of the 11th century and founded a famous theological school; the atlas start of 1080 is earlier than the source suggests.
Died 15 July 1117.

people.name: John Italos
people.bio: Philosopher of Calabrian origin who succeeded Psellos as chief philosopher of Constantinople and was condemned in 1082.

stops.note: Pupil of Michael Psellos; succeeded him as first philosopher of Constantinople. Held court favour under Michael VII (1071-78).
Condemned by a synod and confined to a monastery.

people.name: Constantine the African
people.bio: North African physician who translated Arabic medical works into Latin at Salerno and Monte Cassino.

stops.note: Born in Carthage according to Peter the Deacon; Britannica allows Carthage or Sicily.
At Salerno; Treccani considers his arrival probably earlier than 1076-77.
Monk of Monte Cassino under Abbot Desiderius (1058-1086), where he translated.
Died 22 December; Britannica gives 1087, Treccani says the year is unknown.

people.name: Johannes Afflacius
people.bio: Monk of Monte Cassino and pupil of Constantine the African.

people.name: Irnerius
people.bio: Founder of the Bologna school of Roman law, the first of the glossators.

stops.note: Taught rhetoric, then founded his school of jurisprudence at Bologna in 1084.

people.name: Gratian
people.bio: Monk and canonist at Bologna who compiled the Decretum, the foundation of canon law.

stops.note: Taught at Bologna in the monastery of SS. Felice e Nabore; the Decretum dates from c. 1140.

people.name: Peter Abelard
people.bio: Logician and theologian who taught in the Paris schools and on Mont Sainte-Geneviève.

stops.note: Studied with Roscelin and William of Champeaux.
Lectured at Melun and Corbeil before illness sent him back to Brittany.
Returned to Paris, debated William of Champeaux and taught at several schools (forerunners of the university).
Studied theology under Anselm of Laon.
Master at Notre-Dame until the affair with Héloïse.
Monk of Saint-Denis.
His theology condemned by a synod at Soissons.
Taught and founded the oratory of the Paraclete.
Abbot of Saint-Gildas.
Taught on Mont Sainte-Geneviève in the mid-1130s; the atlas range 1110-1136 also covers his earlier Paris teaching.
Council of Sens condemned nineteen propositions.
Under Peter the Venerable's protection at Cluny and then Saint-Marcel.
Died 21 April 1142.

people.name: Roscelin of Compiègne
people.bio: Logician, an early teacher of Abelard.

people.name: William of Champeaux
people.bio: Paris master and teacher of Abelard.

people.name: Bernard of Chartres
people.bio: Breton master of grammar and logic at the cathedral school of Chartres.

stops.note: Taught logic and grammar from 1114; chancellor of the school from 1119.
Apparently called to teach philosophy in Paris in 1124.

people.name: Thierry of Chartres
people.bio: Master at Chartres and Paris, brother of Bernard of Chartres and teacher of John of Salisbury.

stops.note: Taught at the cathedral school of Chartres alongside his brother Bernard; later its chancellor.

people.name: William of Conches
people.bio: Norman philosopher and grammarian, pupil of Bernard of Chartres, teacher in Chartres and Paris and tutor to the future Henry II.

stops.note: Pupil of Bernard of Chartres.
Taught at Chartres and Paris; tutor to Henry Plantagenet.

people.name: Hugh of St Victor
people.bio: Augustinian canon whose teaching made the school of Saint-Victor in Paris famous.

stops.note: Joined the Augustinian canons of Hamersleben near Halberstadt.
Came to Saint-Victor c. 1115; the school flourished under his guidance from 1133.
Died 11 February 1141.

people.name: Peter Lombard
people.bio: Theologian at the Notre-Dame school in Paris, author of the Sentences and Bishop of Paris.

stops.note: Early schooling at Bologna.
Studied in France at Reims and Paris.
Taught theology at the school of Notre-Dame (the source gives 1136-1150).
Canon of Notre-Dame from 1144-45; taught until 1150 in the Paris schools from which the university grew.
Bishop of Paris from June 1159.
Died 21/22 August 1160.

people.name: Gerard of Cremona
people.bio: Italian translator who rendered some 80 scientific works from Arabic into Latin at Toledo.

stops.note: Went to Toledo to learn Arabic and read Ptolemy's Almagest (translation finished 1175); stayed for the rest of his life. Arrival year approximate.

people.name: Eustathios of Thessalonica
people.bio: Byzantine scholar of Homer who taught rhetoric at the Patriarchal school and became Archbishop of Thessalonica.

stops.note: Monk of the monastery of St Florus.
Taught rhetoric at the Patriarchal school as deacon of Hagia Sophia.
Archbishop of Thessalonica; negotiated with the Normans during the sack of 1185.

people.name: John of Salisbury
people.bio: English scholar, secretary to two archbishops of Canterbury, author of the Policraticus and Bishop of Chartres.

stops.note: About twelve years of study, beginning at Mont-Sainte-Geneviève in 1136.
Secretary to Archbishop Theobald; also at the papal curia under Eugenius III.
Much of the 1160s in exile in France or at the papal court in support of Becket.
Bishop of Chartres.

people.name: Gilbert of Poitiers
people.bio: Theologian and teacher of John of Salisbury; tried at Reims in 1148.

people.name: Robert of Melun
people.bio: Paris master and teacher of John of Salisbury.

people.name: Azo
people.bio: Bolognese glossator of Roman law whose Summa on the Code was the standard work for centuries.

stops.note: Taught civil law at Bologna for at least thirty years; documented 1190-1220. The tradition that he taught at Montpellier rests on a misreading.
Last documented 15 July 1220; a chronicle places his death in 1220.

people.name: Johannes Bassianus
people.bio: Glossator from Cremona, the master of Azo.

people.name: Jacobus Balduini
people.bio: Bolognese jurist, pupil of Azo and principal master of Odofredus.

people.name: Accursius
people.bio: Bolognese jurist, pupil of Azo, who compiled the Glossa ordinaria on the Corpus iuris civilis.

stops.note: Pupil of Azo at Bologna; the source does not date his own teaching (atlas: 1220-1263).

people.name: Odofredus
people.bio: Bolognese teacher of Roman law whose lectures preserve much of the history of the early law school.

stops.note: Studied under Iacopo Baldovini, Ugolino and Bagarotto, before 1229-30.
Was in France before 1234, perhaps in the service of the bishop of Beauvais.
Taught at Bologna until his death; older sources date his start to 1229, unverified.
Died 3 December 1265.

people.name: Robert Grosseteste
people.bio: Oxford master, first lecturer to the Franciscans and Bishop of Lincoln, a pioneer of optics and scientific method.

stops.note: Educated at Oxford.
In the household of William de Vere, bishop of Hereford.
Chancellor of Oxford.
First lecturer in theology to the Oxford Franciscans (1229/30-1235).
Bishop of Lincoln.
Council of Lyon; argued before the papal curia there in 1250.
Died 9 October 1253.

people.name: Roger Bacon
people.bio: English Franciscan philosopher and advocate of experimental science, author of the Opus maius.

stops.note: Studied at Oxford and Paris and taught in the Franciscan school at Oxford, shaped by Grosseteste and Adam Marsh.
Perhaps 11 June 1294 (Britannica: 1292).

people.name: Bonaventure
people.bio: Franciscan theologian at Paris, minister general of his order and cardinal.

stops.note: Pupil of Alexander of Hales at Paris from about 1242 (the atlas start of 1235 is earlier than the source).
Licensed in 1248 to teach as regent; lectures stopped in 1256; doctor with Aquinas in 1257.
Minister General of the Friars Minor from 2 February 1257.
Cardinal-Bishop of Albano.
Died 15 July 1274 during the Second Council of Lyon.

people.name: Alexander of Hales
people.bio: Franciscan master of theology at Paris, teacher of Bonaventure.

people.name: Albertus Magnus
people.bio: Dominican philosopher, theologian and natural scientist, teacher of Thomas Aquinas and founder of the Cologne studium.

stops.note: Likely studied arts at Padua; entered the Dominicans there in 1223.
Studied in Cologne and lectured in the convents of Hildesheim, Freiburg, Regensburg and Strasbourg.
Master of theology at Paris in 1245; taught there until 1248.
Founded and led the Dominican studium generale in Cologne.
Prior Provincial of Teutonia.
Bishop of Regensburg.
Taught in Würzburg and Strasbourg.
Returned to Cologne for good; travelled to Lyon (1274) and Paris (1277).
Died 15 November 1280.

people.name: Thomas Aquinas
people.bio: Dominican theologian and philosopher, master at Paris and author of the Summa theologiae.

stops.note: Born near Aquino; his family held the castle of Roccasecca.
Studied in Naples as a teenager and joined the Dominicans at 19.
Confined by his family for a year.
Studied in Paris, where he met Albert the Great.
Studied under Albert the Great at the new Dominican studium.
Bachelor lecturing on the Sentences, then master and Dominican chair of theology 1256-1259.
Taught in Dominican houses of study in Italy, first at Orvieto.
Then in Rome.
Second regency as master of theology.
Returned to Naples.
Died 7 March 1274 at the Cistercian abbey.

people.name: Robert de Sorbon
people.bio: Chaplain of Louis IX who founded the Sorbonne college for poor theology students in Paris.

stops.note: Born 9 October 1201.
Educated at Reims and Paris.
Canon of Cambrai from 1251; began teaching c. 1253.
Founded the Maison de Sorbonne in 1257; canon of Paris, court chaplain and chancellor of the university from 1258.
Died 15 August 1274.

people.name: Siger of Brabant
people.bio: Paris arts master and leading Aristotelian whose teachings were condemned in 1270 and 1277.

stops.note: Philosophy master at Paris from c. 1260 (first named 1266); prominent until 1276.
Summoned by the French inquisitor in 1276, fled to Italy, probably appealing to the papal court.
Stabbed by a deranged cleric; died between 1281 and 1284.

people.name: George Akropolites
people.bio: Byzantine historian and statesman, grand logothete of the Nicaean emperors and envoy at the Council of Lyon.

stops.note: Reared at the Nicaean court.
Grand logothete from 1255; commanded against Epirus in 1256 and was captured.
Returned to Constantinople after its recapture in 1261 (teaching post per the atlas; Britannica does not describe it).
Represented Michael VIII at the Second Council of Lyon.
Died after an embassy to Trebizond.

people.name: George Pachymeres
people.bio: Byzantine historian, philosopher and teacher at the patriarchal academy of Hagia Sophia.

stops.note: Moved to Constantinople in 1262 (Britannica's date; the atlas gives 1261).
Ordained; taught the liberal arts at the patriarchal academy of Hagia Sophia.

people.name: John Duns Scotus
people.bio: Scottish Franciscan theologian who taught at Oxford, Paris and Cologne.

stops.note: Probably taught philosophy at Cambridge for two years.
Probably in Paris in the Franciscan lectorate program.
Theological study at Oxford (ordained 1291); lectured on the Sentences 1298-99.
Lectured on the Sentences from October 1302.
Expelled from France in June 1303.
Master of theology; regent 1306-1307.
Taught at the Franciscan studium generale in Cologne.
Died 8 November 1308.

people.name: Johannes Andreae
people.bio: Leading canonist of Bologna, author of standard commentaries on the Decretals.

stops.note: Studied civil and canon law; doctor of canon law 1298.
Teaching documented from 1302.
Left for Padua when Bologna's university was suspended by interdict.
Returned to Bologna in autumn 1309.
Died of plague, 7 July 1348.

people.name: Guido da Baisio
people.bio: Canonist at Bologna, the 'Archdeacon', principal teacher of Johannes Andreae.

people.name: Mondino de' Liuzzi
people.bio: Bolognese physician whose Anathomia (1316) became the standard dissection manual.

stops.note: Probably born in Bologna.
First documented lectures 1307-08 (after private teaching with his uncle); city appointments 1321 and 1324.

people.name: Pietro d'Abano
people.bio: Paduan physician and philosopher who sought to reconcile Arabic medicine with natural philosophy.

stops.note: At Paris in the late 1290s, probably teaching; met Ramon Llull there in 1298.
Travelled to Constantinople to learn Greek.
Master at the Padua studium (requested 1306); faced inquisition proceedings.
Died 1315 or 1316.

people.name: William of Ockham
people.bio: English Franciscan logician and political writer who fled Avignon to the court of Ludwig of Bavaria.

stops.note: Given to the London Greyfriars as a boy; began theology c. 1310.
Lectured on the Sentences at Oxford from 1317 without completing his degree.
Disputations at the London Greyfriars.
Summoned to answer charges of heresy.
Fled Avignon with Michael of Cesena to Ludwig of Bavaria.
Died 9/10 April 1347.

people.name: Guy de Chauliac
people.bio: French surgeon, physician to the Avignon popes and author of the Chirurgia magna.

stops.note: Studied at Toulouse, Montpellier, Paris and Bologna; years approximate.
Physician to Pope Clement VI and two successors.
Died 25 July 1368.

people.name: Petrarch
people.bio: Italian poet and humanist scholar who studied law at Montpellier and Bologna.

stops.note: Studied with Convenevole da Prato.
Began law studies.
Studied law until his father's death in 1326.
In the service of the Colonna family.
Settled at Vaucluse; crowned poet in Rome in 1341.
Under the Visconti.
Under the Carrara lords.
Died 18/19 July 1374.

people.name: Francesco Petrarca
people.bio: Italian poet and humanist scholar (Petrarch) who studied law at Montpellier and Bologna.

stops.note: Studied with Convenevole da Prato.
Began law studies.
Studied law until his father's death in 1326.
In the service of the Colonna family.
Settled at Vaucluse; crowned poet in Rome in 1341.
Under the Visconti.
Under the Carrara lords.
Died 18/19 July 1374.

people.name: Convenevole da Prato
people.bio: Exiled Guelph grammar teacher of Petrarch at Carpentras.

people.name: Theodore Metochites
people.bio: Byzantine statesman and scholar who restored the Chora monastery and wrote on astronomy and philosophy.

stops.note: Embassy to the Serbian court.
Grand logothete, directing Byzantine affairs.
Retired to the Chora monastery and directed its restoration (Britannica dates this to 1331; the atlas places his work there from 1316).
Died 13 March 1332.

people.name: Jean Buridan
people.bio: Paris arts master, logician and natural philosopher, twice rector of the university.

stops.note: Studied at the Collège du Cardinal Lemoine; master of arts by the mid-1320s.
Taught arts; rector 1328 and 1340; last documented alive 1358.

people.name: Cino da Pistoia
people.bio: Jurist and poet of the dolce stil novo who taught law at several Italian universities.

stops.note: Studied law at Bologna; doctorate 1314 after six years of exile and political activity.
Taught law at Siena (years per the atlas; the source lists the post without dates).
Taught law at Perugia.
Taught law at Naples.
Returned to Pistoia for the rest of his life.

people.name: Nikephoros Gregoras
people.bio: Byzantine scholar, astronomer and historian, opponent of Hesychasm.

stops.note: Scholar in Constantinople in the circle of Andronicus II; Britannica confirms his court favour and later retreat to a monastery near the capital but does not name the Chora or his teaching there (years per the atlas).
Embassy to King Stefan Uroš III of Serbia.
Excommunicated in 1351 and forced from public life.

people.name: Gentile da Foligno
people.bio: Physician and commentator on Avicenna who taught at Siena and Perugia and died treating plague victims.

stops.note: Commonly believed to have studied medicine at Bologna.
Taught at Siena 22 March 1322 - 30 June 1324.
Invited to Perugia late 1325 (the atlas start of 1322 overlaps his Siena post); attested 1338-1339.
Called to Padua as physician to Ubertino da Carrara c. 1340.
Died 28 June 1348 while treating plague victims.

people.name: Meister Eckhart
people.bio: German Dominican theologian and mystic, twice master at Paris.

stops.note: Probably born in or near Tambach.
Lectured on the Sentences at Paris.
Prior of the Erfurt Dominicans.
Regent master in Paris.
Provincial of Saxonia.
Second Paris regency.
Vicar of the Master General.
In Cologne from 1323-24; heresy proceedings from 1326.
Appealed to the pope.
Probably died 28 January 1328.

people.name: Bartolus de Saxoferrato
people.bio: The most influential commentator on Roman law, professor at Pisa and Perugia.

stops.note: Born near Sassoferrato.
Heard Cino da Pistoia's lectures at about 14.
Bachelor 1333, doctor 10 November 1334.
Assessor at Todi; legal adviser at Macerata in 1338.
Professor at Pisa.
Professor at Perugia until death; met Charles IV at Pisa in 1355.

people.name: Jacopo Butrigario
people.bio: Bolognese jurist who presented Bartolus for his doctorate.

people.name: Nicole Oresme
people.bio: Paris master, Grand Master of the College of Navarre, adviser to Charles V and Bishop of Lisieux.

stops.note: Diocese of Bayeux, possibly at Allemagne.
Master of arts by 1341/42; theology scholar at the College of Navarre in 1348.
Grand Master of the College of Navarre from 1356.
In the service of the dauphin; canon of Rouen 1362, dean 1364.
Bishop of Lisieux.

people.name: John Wyclif
people.bio: Oxford theologian and church reformer whose writings were condemned and inspired the Lollards.

stops.note: Born after 1331 near Richmond, Yorkshire.
Fellow of Merton 1356, master of Balliol 1360, doctor of divinity 1372/73 (the atlas start of 1345 is earlier than the record).
Diplomatic mission.
Left Oxford for Lutterworth.
Died 31 December 1384.

people.name: Leo the Mathematician
people.bio: Byzantine scholar and mathematician who taught at the Magnaura, briefly served as Metropolitan of Thessalonica and headed the Magnaura school founded by Bardas.

stops.note: Educated in Constantinople as a youth.
Learned mathematics from an old monk in the monasteries of Andros.
Taught privately in Constantinople.
Taught at the Magnaura, given a school by Emperor Theophilos.
Metropolitan of Thessalonica, removed when Iconoclasm ended.
Head of the new Magnaura school under Bardas from c. 855 (the atlas gives 849).

people.name: Michael Psellos
people.bio: Byzantine philosopher, historian and courtier who led philosophical teaching in Constantinople as 'Chief of the Philosophers'.

stops.note: Probably born in Constantinople; family from Nicomedia.
Studied under John Mauropous, alongside John Xiphilinos and Constantine Leichoudes; also served as a provincial secretary and judge.
Adviser to Constantine IX and leading professor with the title Chief of the Philosophers (the atlas dates the post from 1046).
Entered the monastery on Mount Olympus.
Recalled to court; key adviser through the reigns of Isaac I, Constantine X and Michael VII.
Most scholars place his death soon after 1078; some argue c. 1096.

people.name: John Mauropous
people.bio: Byzantine poet and teacher, later Metropolitan of Euchaita, who taught Psellos and Xiphilinos.

people.name: John Xiphilinos
people.bio: Byzantine jurist from Trebizond who headed the new law school of Constantinople and became Patriarch John VIII.

stops.note: Studied in Constantinople under John Mauropous.
Nomophylax, head of the law school (years per the atlas; the source gives no dates).
Ecumenical Patriarch 1064-1075.
Died 2 August 1075.

people.name: Ísleifur Gissurarson
people.bio: First bishop of Iceland, educated in Germany, who founded the school at Skálholt.

stops.note: Born to the family that held Skálholt.
Studied at Herford in Germany.
Consecrated bishop of Iceland by Archbishop Adalbert of Bremen.
Built up the see at his family homestead and founded a school there.
Died 5 July 1080.

people.name: Jón Ögmundarson
people.bio: First bishop of Hólar, pupil of Ísleifur at Skálholt.

people.name: Trota of Salerno
people.bio: Twelfth-century woman physician of Salerno, called magistra, author of the Practica secundum Trotam and source for the Trotula texts.

stops.note: Practised medicine at Salerno in the first half of the 12th century; called 'magistra'. Monica Green judges her influence on formal teaching slight.

people.name: Roger Frugardi
people.bio: Salernitan surgeon whose Chirurgia (c. 1180) was the first major surgical textbook of medieval Europe.

stops.note: Salernitan surgeon; wrote the Chirurgia c. 1180. The source does not explicitly say he taught.

people.name: Rolando da Parma
people.bio: Pupil of Roger Frugardi, professor at Bologna, who re-edited his Chirurgia in 1250.

people.name: John of Garland
people.bio: English grammarian and poet who taught in Paris and was among the first masters of the University of Toulouse.

stops.note: Came to Paris in 1202 to complete his studies and stayed as a teacher.
Taught at the new University of Toulouse; fled in 1232 or 1233.
Returned to Paris (the source gives no later posts).

people.name: Nikephoros Blemmydes
people.bio: Byzantine scholar of the Nicaean empire who tutored Theodore II Laskaris and taught George Akropolites.

stops.note: Educated at Prusa, Nicaea, Smyrna and Scamander (under Prodromos) after his family left Constantinople.
Tutored Theodore II Laskaris and taught in a school he founded, where George Akropolites studied.
Retired as a monk to a monastery he built near Ephesus.
Died 1272 (c. 1269 in some accounts).

people.name: Prodromos of Skamandros
people.bio: Teacher of Nikephoros Blemmydes.

people.name: Theodore II Laskaris
people.bio: Emperor of Nicaea, tutored by Nikephoros Blemmydes.

people.name: Jacques de Révigny
people.bio: French jurist of the Orléans school of Roman law, later Bishop of Verdun.

stops.note: Studied law at Orléans under Jean de Monchy, Guichard de Langres and Simon de Paris.
Teaching years per the atlas; the source used does not describe his teaching.
Archdeacon of Toul.
Bishop of Verdun.

people.name: Jean de Monchy
people.bio: Law teacher at Orléans, master of Jacques de Révigny.

people.name: Pierre de Belleperche
people.bio: Orléans law professor who became Chancellor of France under Philip IV and Bishop of Auxerre.

stops.note: Born at the Château de Villars (another source gives 1247).
Professor of civil law at Orléans (years per the atlas).
Councillor in the Parlement, dean of Paris, chancellor and keeper of the seals of Philip IV.
Bishop of Auxerre from 1306, rarely resident.

people.name: Bernard de Gordon
people.bio: Professor of medicine at Montpellier and author of the Lilium medicinae.

stops.note: Teaching at Montpellier before the university charter; the source dates his professorship from 1285.
Professor of medicine; Lilium medicinae dated 1303.

people.name: Arnau de Vilanova
people.bio: Catalan physician, Montpellier master, royal physician and religious reformer.

stops.note: Born in Aragon, probably near Valencia.
Student at Montpellier c. 1260.
Physician to Peter III of Aragon from 1281.
Medical master at the newly chartered studium generale (documented 1291).
Diplomatic mission for James II (DSB supplement corrects 1299 to 1300).
Moved between Provence and Rome.
In the service of Frederick of Trinacria.
Died at sea off Genoa, 6 September 1311.
